The program is at /workspace/dataset/test6_executable and its Python source is:

    import argparse
    from furl import furl
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    parser.add_argument('--a', type=str, required=True)
    parser.add_argument('--b', type=str, required=True)
    parser.add_argument('--c', type=str, required=True)
    args = parser.parse_args()
    f = furl(args.a)
    print(f.scheme)
    print(f.host)
    print(f.path)
    print(f.query.add({args.b: args.c}))
    print(f.url)

Invoke it as:  /workspace/dataset/test6_executable --a "<URL>" --b "<KEY>" --c "<VAL>"
All three args are REQUIRED. It prints exactly 5 lines:
  line1 = f.scheme      (Python None prints as "None"; empty string prints as "")
  line2 = f.host
  line3 = f.path
  line4 = str(f.query) AFTER add({b: c})
  line5 = f.url AFTER that mutation

PROBING TECHNIQUE:
- Use a bash helper so output is unambiguous. Example:
    p(){ echo "IN=[$1] b=[$2] c=[$3]"; /workspace/dataset/test6_executable --a "$1" --b "$2" --c "$3" 2>&1 | cat -A; echo "rc=$?"; }
  cat -A makes trailing spaces / CR / non-ascii visible ($ = end of line, M- sequences = high bytes).
- Use single quotes in bash to avoid shell mangling.
- To distinguish "empty string" from "None" on a line: cat -A shows "$" for empty and "None$" for None.
- Note lines 4 and 5 reflect the MUTATION (the added b=c pair). To see the *original* query you must
  reason by subtracting the appended pair, or use a b/c pair you can recognize (e.g. b=Z c=Z).
- Some inputs may make the program CRASH (traceback) or exit nonzero. Record those exactly:
  the exception type and message matter, but for our port we mainly need to know WHICH inputs crash.
- Run MANY probes (30+). Be systematic: vary one thing at a time. Confirm every rule with at least
  two independent examples, and actively try to FALSIFY each rule you form.

OUTPUT CONTRACT: return findings as structured data. Rules must be precise enough that another engineer
can implement them in JavaScript WITHOUT running the executable. Always attach the literal probe
transcripts (exact argv you passed, exact 5 output lines) that justify each rule.


DIMENSION: SCHEMELESS / RELATIVE / DEGENERATE INPUTS.
From earlier scouting we know: --a "www.google.com" gives scheme=None host=None path=www.google.com,
and --a "" gives scheme=None host=None path=(empty) url="?K=V".
Map this space exhaustively: "www.google.com", "www.google.com/p", "www.google.com:80/p",
"/p", "p", "./p", "../p", "//h/p", "//h", "///p", "?a=1", "?", "#f", "a?b", ":", "::", "@h/p",
"h@x/p", " " (single space), "   ", a string of only ampersands, "http", "http:", "://",
"1.2.3.4/p", "1.2.3.4:80/p", "[::1]/p", "localhost", "localhost/p", "localhost:80".
For each report the exact 5 lines. Determine the precise rule that decides host-vs-path when there is
no scheme, and how f.url is reassembled when host is None (e.g. is a "?" always emitted before the query,
is there ever a stray "//"). This dimension decides many corner cases of the port.

content.text: I have a complete, self-consistent model verified against ~95 probes. Writing up findings.

rules.rule: SCHEME DETECTION runs on the RAW --a string, before any whitespace or control-character processing. Algorithm: (1) if raw.startsWith(':') -> scheme = '' (empty string, prints as blank line). (2) else let prefix = raw truncated at the first occurrence of any of '#', '?', '/'; let i = prefix.indexOf(':'); if i <= 0 -> scheme = null. (3) else let cand = raw.slice(0, i); if cand[0] is NOT an ASCII letter [A-Za-z] -> scheme = null; otherwise scheme = cand.toLowerCase(). Characters after the first are UNRESTRICTED — underscore, space, '%', '@', '~', TAB and NEWLINE are all accepted inside a scheme, unlike RFC/urllib scheme_chars.
rules.evidence:
a='www.google.com:80/p' -> www.google.com|None|80/p|Z=Z|www.google.com:80/p?Z=Z  (dots OK, colon before '/')
a='a_b:c' -> a_b|None|c|Z=Z|a_b:c?Z=Z  (underscore accepted -> NOT urllib scheme_chars)
a='a b:c' -> a b|None|c|Z=Z|a b:c?Z=Z ; a='a%b:c' -> a%b|None|c|Z=Z|a%b:c?Z=Z ; a='a@b:c' -> a@b|None|c|Z=Z|a@b:c?Z=Z ; a='a~b:c' -> a~b|None|c|Z=Z|a~b:c?Z=Z
a=$'ht\ttp://h/p' -> 'ht<TAB>tp'|h|/p|Z=Z|'ht<TAB>tp://h/p?Z=Z'  (TAB survives INSIDE scheme)
FIRST-CHAR REJECTIONS (all give scheme=None): a='1a:b' -> None|None|1a:b|Z=Z|1a:b?Z=Z ; a='+a:b' -> None|None|+a:b|Z=Z|+a:b?Z=Z ; a='_a:b' -> None|None|_a:b|Z=Z|_a:b?Z=Z ; a='.a:b' -> None|None|.a:b|Z=Z|.a:b?Z=Z ; a='~a:b' -> None|None|~a:b|Z=Z|~a:b?Z=Z ; a='0:b' -> None|None|0:b|Z=Z|0:b?Z=Z ; a='-a:b' (via --a=-a:b) -> None|None|-a:b|Z=Z|-a:b?Z=Z ; a='é:b' -> None|None|%C3%A9:b|Z=Z|%C3%A9:b?Z=Z (non-ASCII letter REJECTED, so the test is ASCII-alpha not str.isalpha())
TRUNCATION AT '/','?','#': a='a/b:c' -> None|None|a/b:c|Z=Z|a/b:c?Z=Z ; a='?a:b' -> None|None|(empty)|a%3Ab&Z=Z|?a%3Ab&Z=Z ; a='ab#c:d' -> None|None|ab|Z=Z|ab?Z=Z#c:d ; a='//h:80/p' -> None|h|/p|Z=Z|//h:80/p?Z=Z
LOWERCASING: a='HTTP://H/P' -> http|h|/P|Z=Z|http://h/P?Z=Z ; a='A.B:c' -> a.b|None|c|Z=Z|a.b:c?Z=Z ; a='A B:c' -> a b|None|c|Z=Z|a b:c?Z=Z ; a='WWW.Google.COM:80/p' -> www.google.com|None|80/p|Z=Z|www.google.com:80/p?Z=Z
COLON-PREFIX: a=':' -> ''|None|(empty)|Z=Z|:?Z=Z ; a=':x' -> ''|None|x|Z=Z|:x?Z=Z ; a='::' -> ''|None|:|Z=Z|::?Z=Z ; a=':x:y' -> ''|None|x:y|Z=Z|:x:y?Z=Z ; a='://' -> ''|''|(empty)|Z=Z|:?Z=Z

rules.rule: AFTER scheme detection, define rest = raw.slice(colonIndex+1) if scheme !== null (colonIndex = 0 for the ':'-prefix case, so rest = raw.slice(1)), else rest = raw. Then define modified = (scheme === null) ? raw : ('http:' + rest). path/query/fragment are taken from pythonUrlsplit(modified). This 'substitute http for the real scheme' step is observable: it makes urllib parse the query/fragment for schemes that normally don't, and it makes the tab/newline stripping apply relative to the substituted prefix.
rules.evidence:
a='foo: //h/p' -> foo|None|%20//h/p|Z=Z|foo:%20//h/p?Z=Z   -- modified='http: //h/p'; urllib does NOT lstrip (string starts with 'h'), rest ' //h/p' does not start with '//' so no netloc, path=' //h/p' -> encoded %20//h/p. If rest had been urlsplit alone it WOULD have been lstripped to '//h/p'.
a=$'foo:\t//h/p' -> foo|None|/p|Z=Z|foo:/p?Z=Z   -- modified='http:<TAB>//h/p'; TAB deleted -> 'http://h/p' -> path '/p'. Compare with the space case above: TAB is deleted, space is not.
a='mailto:a@b.com?x=1' -> mailto|None|a@b.com|x=1&Z=Z|mailto:a@b.com?x=1&Z=Z   -- query parsed even though 'mailto' is not in urllib uses_query.
a='www.google.com:80/p' -> www.google.com|None|80/p|... (modified='http:80/p' -> path '80/p')

rules.rule: pythonUrlsplit(s) semantics needed for the port: (a) DELETE every '\t', '\r', '\n' character anywhere in s; (b) LEFT-strip only (never right-strip) every character in the range \x00-\x20 (space, \t, \n, \r, \x0b, \x0c, \x1f, ...); (c) if indexOf(':')>0 and s[0] is ASCII alpha and every char before the colon is in [A-Za-z0-9+.-], consume 'scheme:'; (d) if the remainder starts with '//', netloc = chars up to the next '/', '?' or '#'; (e) split off '#fragment' then '?query'; the rest is path. Trailing whitespace is preserved and later percent-encoded.
rules.evidence:
LEFT-only strip: a=' a' -> None|None|a|Z=Z|a?Z=Z   vs   a='a ' -> None|None|a%20|Z=Z|a%20?Z=Z
a='//h/p  ' -> None|h|/p%20%20|Z=Z|//h/p%20%20?Z=Z ; a='//h/p ' -> None|h|/p%20|Z=Z|//h/p%20?Z=Z
Middle whitespace kept: a='x //h/p' -> None|None|x%20//h/p|Z=Z|x%20//h/p?Z=Z ; a='/ /p' -> None|None|/%20/p|Z=Z|/%20/p?Z=Z ; a='a/ /b' -> None|None|a/%20/b|Z=Z|a/%20/b?Z=Z
Control chars lstripped: a=$'\x0b//h/p' -> None|None|/p|Z=Z|/p?Z=Z ; a=$'\x0chttp://h/p' -> None|None|/p|Z=Z|/p?Z=Z ; a=$'\x1f/p' -> None|None|/p|Z=Z|/p?Z=Z (note: NOT encoded as %1F, so it was stripped)
TAB/NL deleted anywhere: a=$'//h\t/p' -> None|h|/p|Z=Z|//h/p?Z=Z ; a=$'a\n' -> None|None|a|Z=Z|a?Z=Z ; a=$'\ta' -> None|None|a|Z=Z|a?Z=Z
Re-parse after lstrip: a=' http://h/p' -> None|None|/p|Z=Z|/p?Z=Z ; a=' a:b' -> None|None|b|Z=Z|b?Z=Z ; a=' foo://h/p' -> None|None|/p|Z=Z|/p?Z=Z ; a='  http://h/p?q=1#f' -> None|None|/p|q=1&Z=Z|/p?q=1&Z=Z#f
No-scheme-because-colon-at-0: a='   ://h' -> None|None|://h|Z=Z|://h?Z=Z (i=0 is not >0, so ':' stays in the path)

rules.rule: HOST PRESENCE GATE (the single most important rule of this dimension): host/netloc is non-null ONLY IF the RAW rest literally startsWith('//') — tested BEFORE tab/CR/LF deletion and BEFORE the left-whitespace strip. If that test fails, host = None and any authority that pythonUrlsplit(modified) found is SILENTLY DISCARDED (it does not reappear in the path or the url). The host VALUE, when the gate passes, comes from pythonUrlsplit(modified).netloc (i.e. after tab/NL deletion).
rules.evidence:
GATE FAILS but urlsplit would have found netloc='h' -> host None and 'h' VANISHES:
  a=$'\t//h/p' -> None|None|/p|Z=Z|/p?Z=Z
  a=' //h/p' -> None|None|/p|Z=Z|/p?Z=Z ; a='  //h/p' -> None|None|/p|Z=Z|/p?Z=Z
  a=$'/\t/h/p' -> None|None|/p|Z=Z|/p?Z=Z   ('h' authority found by urlsplit, thrown away)
  a=$'/\t/p' -> None|None|(empty)|Z=Z|?Z=Z   (TOTAL LOSS: urlsplit saw netloc='p', path=''; gate fails -> host None, path '' -> url is just '?Z=Z')
  a=$'\t/\t/p' -> None|None|(empty)|Z=Z|?Z=Z  (second example of total loss)
  a=' //h' -> None|None|(empty)|Z=Z|?Z=Z ; a=$'\rhttp://h/p' -> None|None|/p|Z=Z|/p?Z=Z ; a=$'\r\n//h/p' -> None|None|/p|Z=Z|/p?Z=Z
  a=' foo://h/p' -> None|None|/p|Z=Z|/p?Z=Z ; a=$'foo:\t//h/p' -> foo|None|/p|Z=Z|foo:/p?Z=Z ; a='foo: //h/p' -> foo|None|%20//h/p|Z=Z|foo:%20//h/p?Z=Z
GATE PASSES, value comes from post-TAB-deletion urlsplit:
  a='//h/p' -> None|h|/p|Z=Z|//h/p?Z=Z ; a=$'//h\t/p' -> None|h|/p|Z=Z|//h/p?Z=Z (tab gone from host)
  a=$'//\t/p' -> None|''|/p|Z=Z|///p?Z=Z (gate passes on raw '//', urlsplit sees '///p' -> netloc='')
  a='// h/p' -> None|' h'|/p|Z=Z|// h/p?Z=Z ; a='//h /p' -> None|'h '|/p|Z=Z|//h /p?Z=Z (spaces kept verbatim in host)

rules.rule: HOST-vs-PATH decision when there is no scheme, stated plainly: a bare 'www.google.com' or 'localhost' is NEVER a host — it becomes the PATH. host is only non-null when the string (after removing an optional 'scheme:' prefix) begins with a literal '//'. A colon that appears before any '/', '?' or '#' turns the text before it into a SCHEME (not a host) whenever that text starts with an ASCII letter, so 'www.google.com:80/p' parses as scheme='www.google.com', path='80/p'. If it starts with a digit (an IPv4 literal) the whole thing stays in the path.
rules.evidence:
a='www.google.com' -> None|None|www.google.com|Z=Z|www.google.com?Z=Z
a='www.google.com/p' -> None|None|www.google.com/p|Z=Z|www.google.com/p?Z=Z
a='localhost' -> None|None|localhost|Z=Z|localhost?Z=Z ; a='localhost/p' -> None|None|localhost/p|Z=Z|localhost/p?Z=Z
a='localhost:80' -> localhost|None|80|Z=Z|localhost:80?Z=Z ; a='sup.com:8080/p' -> sup.com|None|8080/p|Z=Z|sup.com:8080/p?Z=Z
a='1.2.3.4/p' -> None|None|1.2.3.4/p|Z=Z|1.2.3.4/p?Z=Z ; a='1.2.3.4:80/p' -> None|None|1.2.3.4:80/p|Z=Z|1.2.3.4:80/p?Z=Z (digit-leading => no scheme, all path)
a='[::1]/p' -> None|None|%5B::1%5D/p|Z=Z|%5B::1%5D/p?Z=Z ('[' not a letter => no scheme, brackets percent-encoded into the path)
a='p' -> None|None|p ; a='./p' -> None|None|./p ; a='../p' -> None|None|../p ; a='/p' -> None|None|/p ; a='@h/p' -> None|None|@h/p ; a='h@x/p' -> None|None|h@x/p ; a='http' -> None|None|http|Z=Z|http?Z=Z

rules.rule: HOST PRINTING: host===null prints 'None'. netloc==='' prints an empty line (distinguishable). Otherwise host = netloc with userinfo (everything up to and including the last '@' of the authority) removed and a ':port' suffix removed, then LOWERCASED; IPv6 brackets are KEPT. Non-ASCII hosts print raw (UTF-8) on line 2 but are IDNA/punycode-encoded in f.url on line 5.
rules.evidence:
a='//u:pw@h:8080/x' -> None|h|/x|Z=Z|//u:pw@h:8080/x?Z=Z (userinfo+port stripped from host, preserved in url)
a='//[::1]/p' -> None|[::1]|/p|Z=Z|//[::1]/p?Z=Z (brackets retained)
a='//H.COM/p' -> None|h.com|/p|Z=Z|//h.com/p?Z=Z (lowercased)
a='//h é/p' -> None|'h é'|/p|Z=Z|//xn--h -cja/p?Z=Z (raw on line 2, punycode in url)
Empty vs None: a='///p' -> None|(EMPTY LINE)|/p|Z=Z|///p?Z=Z  vs  a='http:' -> http|None|(empty)|Z=Z|http://?Z=Z

rules.rule: URL REASSEMBLY (line 5). Let S = scheme (null | '' | string), N = netloc (null | '' | string), P = str(path), Q = str(query after add), F = str(fragment). Step 1 — CPython urlunsplit((S||'', N||'', P, Q, F)): `if (N) || (S && USES_NETLOC.has(S) && P.slice(0,2) !== '//') { if (P && P[0] !== '/') P = '/' + P; u = '//' + (N||'') + P } else { u = P }`; `if (S) u = S + ':' + u`; `if (Q) u += '?' + Q`; `if (F) u += '#' + F`. Step 2 — furl fix-ups, in this order and mutually exclusive in practice: `if (S === '') u = ':' + u;` then `if (N === '' && S === null) u = '//' + u;`. Note the '//' re-prefix is gated on scheme being NULL (not merely falsy) — with S==='' no '//' is added.
rules.evidence:
N==='' && S===null -> '//' prefixed: a='//' -> None|''|(empty)|Z=Z|//?Z=Z ; a='///' -> None|''|/|Z=Z|///?Z=Z ; a='///p' -> None|''|/p|Z=Z|///p?Z=Z ; a='////p' -> None|''|//p|Z=Z|////p?Z=Z ; a='//?x=1' -> None|''|(empty)|x=1&Z=Z|//?x=1&Z=Z ; a='//#f' -> None|''|(empty)|Z=Z|//?Z=Z#f
N==='' but S==='' -> NO '//' (the authority marker is LOST): a='://' -> ''|''|(empty)|Z=Z|:?Z=Z ; a='://?x=1' -> ''|''|(empty)|x=1&Z=Z|:?x=1&Z=Z ; a=':///p' -> ''|''|/p|Z=Z|:/p?Z=Z
N==='' but S non-empty & not in USES_NETLOC -> NO '//': a='foo://' -> foo|''|(empty)|Z=Z|foo:?Z=Z ; a='foo:///p' -> foo|''|/p|Z=Z|foo:/p?Z=Z ; a='foo:////p' -> foo|''|//p|Z=Z|foo://p?Z=Z (4 slashes in -> 2 out)
USES_NETLOC branch injects '//' even with N===null: a='http:' -> http|None|(empty)|Z=Z|http://?Z=Z ; a='http:80' -> http|None|80|Z=Z|http:///80?Z=Z (leading '/' inserted then '//' prefixed) ; a='ws:80' -> ws|None|80|Z=Z|ws:///80?Z=Z ; a='http:///p' -> http|''|/p|Z=Z|http:///p?Z=Z ; a='http:////p' -> http|''|//p|Z=Z|http://p?Z=Z (P starts with '//' so the branch is skipped)
Non-USES_NETLOC control: a='foo:80' -> foo|None|80|Z=Z|foo:80?Z=Z ; a='www.google.com:80/p' -> www.google.com|None|80/p|Z=Z|www.google.com:80/p?Z=Z
S==='' prefix ':': a=':' -> ''|None|(empty)|Z=Z|:?Z=Z ; a='::' -> ''|None|:|Z=Z|::?Z=Z ; a=':x' -> ''|None|x|Z=Z|:x?Z=Z ; a='://p' -> ''|p|(empty)|Z=Z|://p?Z=Z

rules.rule: USES_NETLOC (schemes that force a '//' into f.url even with no host) = exactly Python's urllib.parse.uses_netloc: ftp, http, gopher, nntp, telnet, imap, wais, file, mms, https, shttp, snews, prospero, rtsp, rtspu, rsync, svn, svn+ssh, sftp, nfs, git, git+ssh, ws, wss, itms-services. Comparison is on the LOWERCASED scheme. Everything else (foo, mailto, news, ssh, ftps, data, javascript, about, tel, urn, www.google.com, localhost, ...) does not.

IN LIST (a='<scheme>:' -> line5): http -> http://?Z=Z ; https -> https://?Z=Z ; ftp -> ftp://?Z=Z ; file -> file://?Z=Z ; gopher -> gopher://?Z=Z ; imap -> imap://?Z=Z ; nntp -> nntp://?Z=Z ; telnet -> telnet://?Z=Z ; ws -> ws://?Z=Z ; wss -> wss://?Z=Z ; sftp -> sftp://?Z=Z ; svn -> svn://?Z=Z ; git -> git://?Z=Z ; rtsp -> rtsp://?Z=Z ; shttp -> shttp://?Z=Z ; snews -> snews://?Z=Z ; prospero -> prospero://?Z=Z ; wais -> wais://?Z=Z ; rsync -> rsync://?Z=Z ; mms -> mms://?Z=Z ; rtspu -> rtspu://?Z=Z ; svn+ssh -> svn+ssh://?Z=Z ; git+ssh -> git+ssh://?Z=Z ; nfs -> nfs://?Z=Z ; itms-services -> itms-services://?Z=Z
NOT IN LIST: foo -> foo:?Z=Z ; mailto -> mailto:?Z=Z ; news -> news:?Z=Z ; ssh -> ssh:?Z=Z ; ftps -> ftps:?Z=Z ; data -> data:?Z=Z ; javascript -> javascript:?Z=Z ; about -> about:?Z=Z ; tel -> tel:?Z=Z ; urn -> urn:?Z=Z
(all of these had lines 1-4 = '<scheme>' | 'None' | '' | 'Z=Z')

rules.rule: A STRAY '//' WITH host===None IS REACHABLE: it happens when path itself begins with '//' while the host gate failed. Reachable via a 4+-slash sequence broken by a TAB/CR/LF so the raw rest does not literally start with '//'. Conversely, '//' is NEVER emitted for a plain schemeless relative path. And the '?' before the query is ALWAYS emitted whenever the query string is non-empty (which, since {b:c} is always added, is always — the query is at minimum '=' when b and c are both empty).

STRAY '//' with host None: a=$'/\t///p' -> None|None|//p|Z=Z|//p?Z=Z   and   a=$'\t////p' -> None|None|//p|Z=Z|//p?Z=Z
Path-only '//' kept verbatim (no host): a='p//q' -> None|None|p//q|Z=Z|p//q?Z=Z ; a='.//p' -> None|None|.//p|Z=Z|.//p?Z=Z
'?' always present: a='' -> None|None|(empty)|Z=Z|?Z=Z ; a=' ' -> None|None|(empty)|Z=Z|?Z=Z ; a='   ' -> same ; a='  ' -> same ; a=$'\n' -> same ; a='?' -> None|None|(empty)|Z=Z|?Z=Z ; a='#' -> None|None|(empty)|Z=Z|?Z=Z ; a='#f' -> None|None|(empty)|Z=Z|?Z=Z#f ; a='x?' -> None|None|x|Z=Z|x?Z=Z
Empty b and c still yield a non-empty query: a='' b='' c='' -> None|None|(empty)|=|?=   and   a='?' b='' c='v' -> None|None|(empty)|=v|?=v

rules.rule: PATH PERCENT-ENCODING (applies to line 3 and to the path portion of line 5). Existing %XX escapes are decoded and then re-encoded, so %41 -> A while %2F/%3F stay encoded. Characters that get encoded: space->%20, '"'->%22, '%'->%25, '<'->%3C, '>'->%3E, '['->%5B, '\\'->%5C, ']'->%5D, '^'->%5E, '`'->%60, '{'->%7B, '|'->%7C, '}'->%7D, and non-ASCII as UTF-8 %XX%XX. rules.rule: QUERY (line 4) in the degenerate/schemeless case: the pre-existing query string from the input is preserved essentially verbatim (bare keys with no '=' stay bare, empty segments between '&' are preserved, ':' in a key is encoded to %3A), and the new pair 'b=c' is appended with a '&' separator. An input query of '' (from a bare '?' or no '?') contributes nothing, so line 4 is exactly 'b=c'.

uncertainties: The internal decomposition into 'get_scheme on the raw string' + 'modified = http: + rest' + 'urlsplit' is inferred, not read. It reproduces all ~95 probes I ran, but it is a behavioral model. In particular I could not distinguish 'netloc presence = rest.startsWith("//") on the raw rest' from 'netloc presence = the substituted string has // immediately after the scheme colon, tested before tab/NL removal' — both give identical predictions on every probe I could construct. Either is safe to implement.

The scheme first-character test is confirmed as ASCII-letter-only ([A-Za-z]) by 8 rejections and ~15 acceptances, but I did not enumerate every non-letter byte. NUL (\x00) could not be tested because bash cannot pass it in argv.

str(f.path) for a scheme-less input never round-trips the discarded authority, so inputs like $'/\t/p' are irreversibly lossy. I verified two examples but did not enumerate the whole family of tab-broken slash sequences.

The exact percent-encoding set for the path was sampled (~30 characters), not exhaustively enumerated. Characters I did not test include the remaining C1/high-bit ranges beyond one UTF-8 example (é) and delimiters like '?' and '#' appearing pre-encoded as %3F/%23 in the middle of a segment (I only tested %2F and %3F).

Non-ASCII host handling (IDNA punycode in f.url, raw UTF-8 on line 2) was observed once ('//h é/p' -> 'xn--h -cja'). The exact IDNA variant (idna vs uts46, and what happens on IDNA failure such as an over-long label or a leading hyphen) is unexplored and may be another crash source; it belongs to the host dimension rather than this one.

f.query was always non-empty in my probes because {b: c} is always added (minimum '='), so I could never observe whether f.url omits the '?' for an empty query. A JS port should still implement 'emit ? only if the query string is non-empty' for safety.

I did not test whether an input with BOTH a fragment and an empty path plus an empty netloc ('' host) interacts with the '//' re-prefix in some order-dependent way beyond the '//#f' case; the ':' prefix (scheme==='') and the '//' prefix (netloc==='' and scheme===null) are mutually exclusive in every reachable state I found, but I proved that only by construction, not exhaustively.
